verses.text: The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,
“Arise, and go down to the potter’s house, and there I will cause you to hear my words.”
Then I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was making a work on the wheels.
When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
“House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” says Yahweh. “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up and to break down and to destroy it;
if that nation, concerning which I have spoken, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do to them.
At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to build and to plant it;
if they do that which is evil in my sight, that they not obey my voice, then I will repent of the good, with which I said I would benefit them.

“Now therefore, speak to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, ‘Yahweh says: “Behold, I frame evil against you, and devise a device against you. Everyone return from his evil way now, and amend your ways and your doings.”’
But they say, ‘It is in vain; for we will walk after our own devices, and we will do everyone after the stubbornness of his evil heart.’”
Therefore Yahweh says: “Ask now among the nations, who has heard such things. The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing.
Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? Shall the cold waters that flow down from afar be dried up?
For my people have forgotten me. They have burned incense to false gods. They have been made to stumble in their ways, in the ancient paths, to walk in byways, in a way not built up;
to make their land an astonishment, and a perpetual hissing. Everyone who passes thereby shall be astonished, and shake his head.
I will scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy. I will show them the back, and not the face, in the day of their calamity.

Then they said, “Come, and let us devise devices against Jeremiah; for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not give heed to any of his words.”
Give heed to me, Yahweh, and listen to the voice of those who contend with me.
Shall evil be recompensed for good? For they have dug a pit for my soul. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them, to turn away your wrath from them.

Therefore deliver up their children to the famine, and give them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives become childless, and widows; and let their men be slain of death, and their young men struck by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses, when you shall bring a troop suddenly on them; for they have dug a pit to take me, and hidden snares for my feet.

Yet, Yahweh, you know all their counsel against me to kill me. Don’t forgive their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from your sight; but let them be overthrown before you. Deal you with them in the time of your anger.

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks to Jeremiah—not in vague feelings, but a clear word. How often we ask for direction, yet when it comes plainly, we hesitate. The Word that comes is both gift and test.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Down to the potter's house—an ordinary place where clay is shaped. Sometimes the Lord teaches us not in the temple or by firelight, but in workshops and common streets. He meets us where the real work happens.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah watches. The potter's wheel spins, fingers shaping the clay—a picture of intention, skill, and presence. We live in a world that feels chaotic, yet here is One whose hands know exactly what they are doing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The vessel breaks. The potter does not discard it or curse the failure—he begins again. There is mercy in being re-formed, in not being thrown away. The Lord has never seen a broken life as waste.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word comes again—now Jeremiah understands what he has seen. The Lord explains His own parable. He does not leave us guessing; He speaks the meaning into our hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As clay in the potter's hand—so Israel, and so are you. This is not menace but invitation to trust. Being clay means you are not alone, not abandoned to random pressure, but held by One whose purpose is to shape, not to break.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks His sovereignty: He frames judgment with intention. Not cruelty, but deliberation. And always—even before it falls—there is space for repentance, for the possibility of turning away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If the nation turns, the judgment turns with it. The Lord's heart moves toward mercy the moment we move toward Him. This is not weakness in God, but the deepest strength: He wants to forgive.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Similarly, He speaks promise. He plans to build and plant—good things. Yet even these come with condition, with the weight of covenant. The Lord does not scatter mercy carelessly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If they do evil, He repents of the good He intended. The Lord is not bound to bless stubbornness. He grieves when He must hold back what He longs to give. This is the sorrow of a Father who is also Judge.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Go tell them plainly: I have framed evil against you, yet still—amend your ways. The message is both warning and plea. Even judgment is an act of love when it calls us back to the path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: And they refuse. 'It is in vain'—these bitter words from a stubborn heart. They choose their own devices over the Lord's. How it must grieve Jeremiah to speak a word that falls on ears already closed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The virgin of Israel has done a horrible thing. A tender people has hardened into something unrecognizable, unfaithful. Sometimes we must name the weight of our own rebellion to feel the weight of His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The snow of Lebanon, the waters flowing from afar—these are constants, reliable. Yet Israel forgets that they, too, are meant to be constant in their loyalty. The created order keeps faith; why do we struggle to?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They have forgotten the Lord and burned incense to false gods. And now they stumble in paths not built up, byways. When we forget Him, we leave the main road. Every wandering begins with a small forgetting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land becomes astonishment, a perpetual hissing—a warning to all who pass. Ruin speaks louder than any sermon. Yet even in desolation, there is a silent call: see what happens when we turn from God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will scatter them with an east wind, show them My back, not My face. Being hidden from God's face is the deepest exile. Yet even in this verse lies a hidden mercy: He does not say it is forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Then they plot against Jeremiah himself—strike him with the tongue. The prophet pays a price for speaking God's word. His enemies fear not the message itself, but the one who will not be silent. Such is the lot of the faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah cries out to the Lord: Give heed to me, listen to those who contend with me. When we are attacked for righteousness, we do not plead for revenge first—we plead for the Lord's attention. He hears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shall evil be recompensed for good? Jeremiah has interceded for them, yet they plot his death. The sting is that he spoke for their blessing and receives only malice. Yet standing faithfully through ingratitude is its own crown.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Deliver them to famine, sword, bereavement—Jeremiah's prayer is fierce, invoking judgment. His suffering is real, his anger justified. Yet he leaves vengeance with the Lord. Even in rage, the faithful rest their case with Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They have dug a pit for me, hidden snares—yet Jeremiah remains. They plot, but he does not flee the office. This is the steadfastness of one who knows his calling comes from above the schemes of men.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah calls on the Lord: You know all their counsel against me. Readers today hear an echo in this—how the Lord knows what is plotted in secret, and though we cannot see it, He is fully aware and sovereign. As of 2026-10, many of us know the comfort of being seen and known by God when the world's schemes swirl unseen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
